ruleName: Deliberately Changing Club's Performance Characteristics During Round
imagePrompt: Create a polished, modern semi-realistic (75% realistic, 25% stylised) illustration of a golfer on a golf course tee box, preparing to adjust the loft of their adjustable driver using a manufacturer's adjustment tool. The golfer is dressed in typical golf attire and is holding both the driver and the adjustment tool, with the golf ball teed up in front of them. Capture the moment just before the adjustment, making the situation and tools clear. The background shows the course environment. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards, or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer on a tee box about to adjust the loft on their driver using an adjustment tool, with a golf ball teed up in front, illustrating a rules scenario about adjusting clubs during play.

sceneSpec.setting: On a golf course tee box during a friendly round, with typical course features visible in the background.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer, dressed in standard golf attire, holding an adjustable driver and an adjustment tool in hand.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Golf ball is resting on a tee in front of the golfer on the tee box.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment just before the golfer uses the adjustment tool to change the loft setting on their adjustable driver.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Illustrate a player adjusting the playing characteristics of a club during a round, which is not permitted.

questions.title: Can You Change Your Driver?
questions.question: You are playing and want to make your driver hit the ball higher. You take out a tool and change the driver’s loft during your round. Are you allowed to do this?

choices.text: Yes. You can change your clubs whenever you want during the round.
Yes, but only when you are walking between holes.
No. You can’t change how your club plays once your round has started.
Yes, but only if you change the loft once.

questions.explanation: You are not allowed to change your club to make it work differently during your round. For example, you can’t use a tool to make your driver hit the ball higher after you start playing. You can only make these changes before you start your round.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Loft is the angle of the clubface that helps decide how high the ball goes.
The driver is a club used to hit the ball a long way, often at the start of a hole.

questions.teachingTip: Explain that the Rules want everyone to play with the clubs they start with—not to change them during the round.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children may think they can use tools to change their clubs during play if they see someone else do it.
They may believe small changes, like changing just once, are okay.

questions.title: Adjusting Your Driver During the Round
questions.question: Halfway through your round, you decide to increase the loft of your adjustable driver using the manufacturer's adjustment tool to help get the ball higher in the air. Is this allowed?

choices.text: Yes. You may adjust your clubs at any time during the round.
No. Deliberately changing the playing characteristics of a club during a round is not allowed.
Yes, provided you only change the loft once.

questions.explanation: If a club has adjustable features, such as an adjustable loft or lie, those settings must not be changed during a round. Altering the club's playing characteristics after the round has started is a breach of the Rules. You may only adjust the club before the round begins. If a club is damaged during normal play, it may be repaired or replaced in certain circumstances, but you cannot use the adjustment mechanism to change how the club is designed to play. (Rule 4.1a(3))
